investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-29T10:41–10:48Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node cluster has zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), causing every remote-agent pod to remain Unschedulable for ~143–147 seconds before the eval times out. No required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never started.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. As a result, no new remote-agent pod can be scheduled, the VM is never provisioned, and the eval probe cannot collect any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity or configuration failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes scheduling path; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval.

investigations.title: Image Generation Eval Failure: OpenAI Billing Hard Limit Reached on /api/generate/image/stream
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API returned a hard billing limit error (billing_hard_limit_reached) when the eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream. The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of a generation_completed frame, causing both required contract assertions to fail: frameTypes did not contain "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent remained false.
investigations.rootCause: The OpenAI account or API key used by the eval runner has hit its configured billing hard limit. The upstream API rejected the image generation request before any image could be produced, causing the /api/generate/image/stream SSE endpoint to emit a generation_error frame with code GENERATION_FAILED and the message "Billing hard limit has been reached." (error code: billing_hard_limit_reached, type: billing_limit_user_error). This is an external dependency failure at the OpenAI billing layer, not a code defect in the eval runner or the AURA image generation route itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval infrastructure failure scoped to the observability check environment.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=451 — the request returned in under half a second, consistent with an immediate API rejection rather than a generation timeout.

investigations.title: model-matrix eval failure: aura-gpt-5-5 returns 502/424 provider_account_unavailable
investigations.summary: The model-matrix eval failed because the runtime test call for model aura-gpt-5-5 returned a 502 Bad Gateway wrapping a 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable, causing 1 of 2 models to fail and violating the allPassed=true and failedModelCount=0 contract assertions. investigations.rootCause: The upstream provider backing aura-gpt-5-5 was unreachable at the time of the eval run (2026-07-29T10:40:38–50Z). AURA's harness runtime returned HTTP 424 Failed Dependency with code provider_account_unavailable and the message "AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits." This is a provider-side or AURA-side connectivity/availability issue scoped to the aura-gpt-5-5 model route, not a misconfiguration of the eval itself. All required evidence fields were present and the eval infrastructure executed correctly; only the runtime response for aura-gpt-5-5 was non-OK.

AURA-side routing or proxy layer failure for the aura-gpt-5-5 model route specifically — the 502 Bad Gateway is emitted by AURA's harness before the 424 is surfaced, suggesting the AURA gateway could not forward the request; however the error message attributes the issue to provider reachability.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-29T10:41–10:48Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node cluster has zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), causing every remote-agent pod to remain Unschedulable for ~143–147 seconds before the eval times out. No required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never started.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. As a result, no new remote-agent pod can be scheduled, the VM is never provisioned, and the eval probe cannot collect any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity or configuration failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes scheduling path; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval.

Preemption is also blocked ('No preemption victims found'), indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If the selector was recently tightened or node labels were changed, capacity would drop sharply.

Tertiary — kata-containers / peer-pods infrastructure issue: the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource may not be correctly advertised by the node device plugin on the 2 eligible nodes, causing the reported count to be lower than actual hardware capacity.

Quaternary — leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval runs or user sessions did not clean up their pods, slots remain occupied. The runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs:1883) but a prior failed cleanup could leave orphaned pods.
